debug.exported:
**Debug file created**

1. Download it: {download} (the link works for {hours} hours, the file is also saved as `{file}` in the config folder).
2. [Open a GitHub issue]({issue}) - the version and the time are filled in.
3. Describe what happened, when it happened and what you expected, and drag the file into the field *Debug file*.

Create the file as soon as possible after the problem: it holds the latest calculations and log messages.

The file contains your settings, prices, energy history and plans, the blueprint automations and the integrations and device models you use. Names, entity names, serial numbers, coordinates, notify services, addresses and keys are removed or replaced. Nothing is sent anywhere - you decide what you upload.

entity_help.soc_charge_power: The model learns from stable raw history measurements with a constant phase count in CJP's recorded per-phase amp settings. These are not separate measurements of current in each physical phase. A SOC band limits the plan only when power is at least 10% lower than at lower SOC in the same session across at least 3 separate sessions. The comparison reduces, but cannot remove, the influence of the charger, solar or site limits. Unknown phases, unstable readings and SOC bands without enough data keep the existing capacity assumption. Until a band has its own measurements, stable hourly long-term statistics give start values, marked 📊; they only count where the phase count is certain (a 1-phase charger, or above 3.8 kW on a 3-phase charger). The cap changes only the power calculated by the plan, not charger control.
entity_help.learn_distance: Distance suggestions are calculated from the odometer over the last 8 weeks, even when this switch is off. When on, Work Plan uses the higher of the entered and learned distance for each weekday (at least 3 measured days for that weekday). Optimal weekly charging uses the learned typical daily distance (at least 14 measured days). Learned values affect the plan only while the corresponding charging rule is active. Entered values are never changed; suggestions appear in the learned_distance attributes.
entity_help.public_charging:
When a public charging session ends (charge port/cable used away from home), Public charging session done turns on and you get a notification.
• Enter the total amount in Public charging session cost.
• The session is added to the charging history about 1 min after entering it.
• Enter -1 to ignore the session.
entity_help.forced_charging:
Forced charging can be enabled manually when the battery level is under the daily minimum.
• Charging: charges up to the daily minimum ({min_daily_battery_level} %).
• Cost control: no charging in the most expensive hours (see the attribute expensive_hours).
entity_help.manual_charging:
Manual charging starts charging at once without waiting for the plan.
• Allow manual charging now: charges with max current from the grid and solar.
• Solar only: charges only with the solar surplus.
Both are turned off automatically when the car is plugged in again.
entity_help.cheap_targets:
Charge targets at cheap prices:
• Very cheap target ({charge_very_cheap_battery_level} %): when the price is at most the average of the cheapest known prices of the coming week.
• Ultra cheap target ({charge_ultra_cheap_battery_level} %): when the price is another 25 % lower.
The targets follow the expected solar surplus of the coming week.
entity_help.trip:
Trip charging is planned automatically when:
• Trip charge percent is above 0 %, or Trip range needed is above 0 {distance}.
• Trip departure and Trip homecoming are set in the future.
It charges what the trip needs (from the percent or the distance). Charging between {max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level}-100 % happens in the last hours before departure (done with the buffer before departure) to protect the battery. If the target cannot be reached, it charges what it can in the buffer.
Trip reset clears the trip; it is also reset automatically 2 hours after departure.
entity_help.solar_charging:
Enabled when there is solar surplus.
• Charging: uses the surplus; switches between 1 and 3 phases depending on it.
• Need: follows the surplus compared to the house consumption. Max charge {max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %.
• Available solar power: shows the power available in watts during the current hour.
• Plan: the expected surplus of the week is used by Optimal weekly charging and Work plan charging, so the car charges as much solar as possible.

{charging_amps_table}
entity_help.fill_up:
Optimal weekly charging can be used on holiday (ignores the work plan).
 Every day: always enough for the typical daily distance ({typical_daily_distance} {distance}) plus the daily minimum ({min_daily_battery_level} %), in the cheapest hours of the day.
The rest up to the max recommended ({max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %) only in the cheapest hours of the week (the cheapest 30 %), and only when the next 24 hours are not clearly cheaper.
entity_help.workplan:
Work plan charging: enable when you work within the next week.
• Charging: plans daily charging over a week from workdays and days off.
• Need: uses departure and homecoming time and the distance of every workday. Minimum battery level at homecoming {min_daily_battery_level} %, max charge {max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %.
• Plan: picks the cheapest available times before the workday departure; whether the target is reached depends on the charging windows and the amount of charging needed.
entity_help.full_charge: Recommended full charge: with an LFP battery a full charge is recommended at least every 14 days or as the car maker says. Set the number of days here; the last full charge is registered automatically.
entity_help.charging_loss:
Charging loss calculation – best result when charging from a low level (e.g. 10 %) to 100 %:
1. Discharge the car as much as possible (max 20 %).
2. Set the wanted charge limit in the car and Max recommended charge limit (now {max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %, at least 90 %).
3. Turn on Calculate charging loss and let the car report when it is full.
4. The result is saved in the options automatically and you get a notification.
entity_help.cheap_limits:
Charge level at cheap prices:
• Very cheap: when the price is at most the average of the cheapest known prices of the coming week, charge to {very_cheap_grid_charging_max_battery_level} %.
• Ultra cheap: when the price is another 25 % lower, charge to {ultra_cheap_grid_charging_max_battery_level} %.
Used by planned charging hours at these prices, and always when "Charge on cheap power" is enabled.
entity_help.battery_preheat:
Battery level and preheating settings:
• Minimum daily battery level ({min_daily_battery_level} %): on returning from work or daily driving.
• Minimum trip battery level ({min_trip_battery_level} %): at homecoming from a trip.
• Minimum charge limit ({min_charge_limit_battery_level} %): the lowest charge limit the car allows.
• Max recommended charge limit ({max_recommended_charge_limit_battery_level} %): the car maker's recommendation.
• Preheat X min before ({preheat_minutes_before} min): preheat before leaving for work and trips (the preheat switch per weekday). In frost, the lead time is doubled.
entity_help.powerwall:
Home battery settings:
• Solar surplus only charges the car when the home battery is above the limit (now {ev_charge_after_powerwall_battery_level} %).
• Use the home battery for the car: needs Solar charging and Home battery discharge above needed turned on; only energy above the limit is used.
Create an automation that disables home battery discharging while the car charges, and only allows it when the switch is on and the battery is above the limit.
entity_help.virtual_ev:
Virtual EV (without a car integration):
• Battery level: set the current battery level of the car when you plug it in.
• Completed battery level: the level the car stops at.
• Estimated total range: the realistic max range of the car.
entity_help.simulated_battery_level:
Simulated battery level (the car updates its battery level slowly):
• Car battery level: the value the car last reported.
• Simulated battery level: the car's last value plus what the charger's kWh meter has counted since, minus the charging loss. The plan and the charger actions use this one.
• When the car reports a new battery level, the simulation is corrected to the car's value (so it can jump a little) and keeps rising from there.
• You can enter the car's real battery level in Simulated battery level yourself, e.g. when you plug in and the car's value is behind. The simulation keeps rising from there until the car reports a new value. When you plug in, a notification asks if the value is right.
• The simulation stops 1 % below the car's charge limit, so the car itself confirms that charging is done.
• If it jumps a lot at every correction, the charging loss is off: measure it under Charging loss.
Turn it on or off in the integration's options under EV - sensors.
entity_help.forecast_auto: Choose the forecast type automatically: the house consumption and the car's distance per kWh each use the forecast type that was most accurate (the house consumption the last 30 days after 7 days of measurements, the distance per kWh the last 30 drives after 10 drives) and only switch when another type has at least 5 % less error. The selected forecast type is the starting point and is always used for the fallback prices and the solar history. See *Forecast accuracy* in the analysis.
entity_help.price_forecast: Correct the price forecast: the plan corrects the forecast prices (e.g. Carnot) with how far off they were the last 30 days, per day ahead – after 7 days of measurements, at most ±0.50 {valuta}. See *Price forecast* in the analysis.

dashboard.help_problem:
**A crash or error** (an error notification, *Error* as the charging rule, entities that stay unavailable) **or a wrong decision** (it charged when it shouldn't have (or didn't when it should), charged too much or too little, or the charging rule looks wrong):

1. Press **Export debug info** below **as soon as possible** - the file holds the latest calculations and log messages, older ones are replaced as time goes by.
2. A notification appears. Download the file and open the GitHub issue from the link in it (version and time are filled in).
3. Describe what happened and **when** (the time), which rule and charger action were shown, and what you expected instead. A screenshot of the plan helps.
4. Drag the file into the field *Debug file*.

The file is anonymised: no names, passwords, API keys, coordinates or addresses, entity names are replaced. Nothing is sent by itself - you decide what you upload.
dashboard.pc_queue: Public charging sessions waiting for their cost
dashboard.pc_enter: Enter the cost of the top session below, then the next one is shown.
dashboard.pc_auto_added: Added to the history automatically ~1 min after entering it.
dashboard.manual_charging_intro: For guests, or when you just want to charge right away – without waiting for the plan.
dashboard.forced_charging_off: *Turn it off again when the battery is above the minimum – it is also turned off automatically the next time the car is plugged in.*
dashboard.loss_intro: Measured continuously from the charger's kWh meter and the car's battery level, also back in Home Assistant's history. Only parts with the same power and phases all the way count.
dashboard.loss_no_data: No measurements yet – the plan uses the configured charging loss
dashboard.loss_one_group: Measurements at one power only so far – the model cannot tell the fixed use from the percentage loss. The loss at that power
dashboard.loss_low_high_2: more energy at the lowest power than at the highest.
dashboard.loss_parts_title: What the loss is made of
dashboard.loss_explain: *Loss = fixed use (the car's electronics while charging) ÷ power + percentage loss. That is why a low power (solar on 1 phase) loses the most. A wrong battery size only moves the loss percentage – the plan still fits your setup. With "Use measured charging loss" on the plan uses the measured loss – otherwise the configured one.*
dashboard.loss_analysis_explain: The chart shows how charging loss changes with charging power and compares measurements with the loss model.
dashboard.loss_kwh_per_percent: Measured: kWh from the charger per 1 %
dashboard.economy_intro: What the charging cost, compared with the same kWh charged in other ways while the car was plugged in at home. Solar and the home battery count with their value like in the plan.
dashboard.economy_subscription_intro: Compares each completed month's recorded charging-history cost with the fixed monthly price above. Solar and the home battery keep the same economic value as elsewhere in CJP. A positive difference means the subscription would have been cheaper. Only sessions recorded in CJP are included; public charging that was never recorded cannot be counted.
dashboard.economy_subscription_explain: Fixed monthly charging price: 0 disables the comparison. Only completed months are compared. The recorded cost includes solar and the home battery at their CJP economic value, so it is not necessarily the cash amount on the electricity bill. The comparison only covers sessions recorded in CJP; missing history can understate a month's cost. The price belongs to this car; do not enter the full price on several cars when one subscription covers them together.
dashboard.what_if_explain: A simulated comparison based on the history CJP has recorded. It never changes the live plan, the settings, the car or the charger, and it is an estimate, not a guaranteed or actual saving. The price field sets the subscription (0 disables it) and the table below compares it with each completed month.
dashboard.what_if_subscription_off: Enter a fixed monthly charging price above to compare it with the recorded charging cost.
dashboard.what_if_subscription_empty: No recorded charging months yet, so there is nothing to compare with the fixed monthly price.
dashboard.what_if_a_title: Daily smart charging to the maximum recommended level
dashboard.what_if_a_explain: Replays your recorded history to compare two ways of charging at home. **Smart** charges in the cheapest hours of every connection until the target level before departure; **Immediate charging** charges from plug-in to the same target. Both use the same driving, public charges, connection periods, charging loss, learned charging power by battery level and hourly grid prices, and carry the battery level from one connection to the next. Settings: the **period** (7-365 days); a temporary **target** (0 uses the live maximum recommended level and never changes it); the **battery level at the first plug-in** (0 reads it from Home Assistant history, otherwise enter it); and the **days** smart charging is applied on (the other days are charged immediately in both). Press **Run what-if** to calculate. Nothing changes in the plan, the settings, the car or the charger. A negative difference means smart charging was cheaper. The adjusted difference values any battery level difference at the end at the period average price. This is a hindsight estimate, not a guaranteed or actual saving: smart knows every price in advance. Only completed connections with hourly prices that CJP stored itself are used, and the replay stops at the first missing price. Not included: solar, house limits, standby drain, small drives CJP did not record, a departure buffer and charging that CJP did not record. CJP recorded cost is shown only as a reference because it includes solar and is not comparable. The result sensor holds the details. Below the settings the card shows the period, the target and where the starting level came from; both calculations side by side; a table per month; the coverage (connections replayed, drives, public charges and missing price hours); warnings about data that was left out or could not be verified; and a fold-out with the assumptions. The day selection refers to the day the car leaves (the end of the connection). The learned charging power by battery level is used only when learning of charging power is switched on. Public charges are already inside the battery use of the drive they belong to, so they are counted but not added again. The work plan days are the days as they are set now, not as they were in the past. With Selected days, switch on the days below the day selection. The table shows, for both calculations, the cost, the energy from the charger, the charging loss, how many connections reached the target, what is missing to the target, the driving that could not be covered, and the lowest and final battery level. If the two calculations do not deliver the same, no difference is shown and the card says why.

dashboard.what_if_b_explain: Replays your recorded history to compare your **current settings** with an **alternative daily reserve** and/or **maximum recommended level**. The reserve is the battery level the car should still have when it comes home; the maximum is the highest level CJP plans to charge to. For each connection the replay charges in the cheapest hours to the level the next recorded drive needs plus the reserve, never above the maximum (a drive that needs more than the maximum is still covered). Both settings use the same driving, connection periods, charging loss, learned charging power by battery level and hourly grid prices, and carry the battery level from one connection to the next. Settings: the **period** (7-365 days) and the **battery level at the first plug-in** (0 reads it from Home Assistant history, otherwise enter it), both shared with the calculation above; the **alternative reserve** and the **alternative maximum level** (0 uses the current setting and never changes it). Press **Run what-if settings** to calculate. Nothing changes in the plan, the settings, the car or the charger. The current settings are replayed as they are now; earlier settings are not stored, so this is not the plan CJP made at the time. This is a simplified model of CJP's planning rule, not CJP's planner: cheap-hour top-ups, forced charging below the reserve, solar, house limits, standby drain and a departure buffer are not included, and the next drive is known in advance (hindsight), which flatters a low reserve. The latest connection is left out because the drive after it is unknown. The reserve may have no effect when the maximum level already decides the level, for example when a drive plus the reserve is above the maximum. A negative difference means the alternative was cheaper. The adjusted difference values any battery level difference at the end at the price per kWh that was actually paid for that energy, because a lower reserve ends lower; the table per month shows the plain cost difference, and only when the two settings are comparable. If the two settings do not cover the same driving, no difference is shown and the card says why. The table shows, for both settings, the reserve and maximum level, the cost, the energy from the charger, the charging loss, the driving that could not be covered, and the lowest and final battery level; the homecomings below the current reserve and the lowest homecoming level are judged against the current reserve for both, so they compare like for like. Below it are a table per month, the coverage (connections replayed, drives, public charges and missing price hours), warnings about data that was left out or could not be verified, and a fold-out with the assumptions. Above the table the card shows the period and where the starting level came from; if a price is missing the replay stops there and the card says where and why, and it shows when a calculation is running or could not be completed, with the previous result kept. The learned charging power by battery level is used only when learning of charging power is switched on. Public charges are already inside the battery use of the drive they belong to, so they are counted but not added again. A value of 0 means the current setting, so a reserve of exactly 0 % cannot be tried; use 1 for practically none. The result sensor holds the details. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed or actual saving.
dashboard.what_if_reason_no_change: Nothing to compare: both alternative values are 0 or equal to the current settings. Enter a different reserve or maximum level
dashboard.what_if_reason_invalid_settings: A reserve or maximum level is outside the allowed range
dashboard.what_if_reason_too_few_windows: At least two completed connections are needed, because the drive after the last one is unknown
dashboard.what_if_note_modelled_policy: A simplified model of the CJP planning rule, not of the CJP planner: charge in the cheapest hours to the next drive plus the reserve, capped at the maximum level.
dashboard.what_if_note_demand_from_recorded_drives: The demand is the recorded next drive, known in advance.
dashboard.what_if_note_settings_history_not_stored: The current settings are replayed. Earlier settings are not stored, so this is not the plan CJP made at the time.
dashboard.what_if_note_last_connection_left_out: The latest connection is left out because the drive after it is not known yet.
dashboard.what_if_note_extra_top_ups_not_modelled: Cheap-hour top-ups above the maximum level are not modelled.
dashboard.what_if_note_forced_low_battery_charging: Forced charging when plugged in below the reserve is not modelled.
dashboard.what_if_d_title: EV solar energy replaced by grid energy
dashboard.what_if_d_explain: Shows what the energy your EV took from solar would have cost if the EV had charged at the same times from the grid instead and the solar had been exported. It is a simulated comparison from the sessions CJP recorded; it never changes the plan, the settings, the car or the charger, and it is an estimate, not an actual or guaranteed saving. For every finished private charging session with solar energy, the same kWh are priced twice: at the hourly grid buy price minus the refund (what CJP prices its grid energy at), and at the sale the solar energy replaced, valued the way CJP values it (the hourly sell price, or the difference to your fixed production price). Solar energy is never treated as free. The solar advantage is the first minus the second; positive means solar was cheaper than the grid. The table shows per month the number of sessions, the solar energy, the two values and the advantage; the total adds only completed months, and the current month is marked incomplete and not added. Both prices are the time-weighted average over the session, which assumes the solar energy was spread evenly over it. The recorded cost of a session is not used, because it is one snapshot price for the whole session. Below the table the card shows how many sessions were left out and why (public charging, still charging, unreadable data such as an end time, no solar energy, recorded before solar energy was stored as energy, not priced in time, or a missing stored buy or sell price), the home battery energy that was kept as recorded, since when the solar energy and the sell prices are stored, and a fold-out with the assumptions. No price is ever filled in: a session without a stored price for every hour is left out. CJP stores sell prices, and the solar energy as energy, from the first run of this comparison, so existing history gives no result and the table fills as new solar sessions are recorded. Each session is priced once, soon after it ends, and kept, because CJP later merges its charging history per day. This is only the first no-solar mode (the EV's solar exported instead). It is not physically no solar production and not a replanned charging without solar, and the home battery is not replaced, so no whole-house result is claimed. The result sensor holds the details.
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_solar_configured: Solar is not set up in CJP, so there is no solar energy to replace
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_price_provider: No price provider is set up, so the refund on the buy price is unknown
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_waiting_for_new_session: Nothing to show yet: solar energy is only usable for sessions recorded after it was stored as energy, so this fills as new solar sessions are recorded
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_sell_prices: No sell prices are stored yet for the sessions with solar: CJP stores them hour by hour from the first run of this comparison, and this fills as hours pass
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_buy_prices: No buy prices are stored for the sessions with solar
dashboard.what_if_d_reason_no_solar_sessions: No finished charging session with solar energy has been recorded
dashboard.what_if_d_left_before_energy_fix: recorded before solar energy was stored as energy
dashboard.what_if_d_left_not_captured: not priced in time (merged into the daily history first)
dashboard.what_if_d_powerwall: Home battery energy in these sessions, kept as recorded and not replaced
dashboard.what_if_d_note_ev_solar_exported_instead: The EV charges at the same times from the grid instead and the solar energy is exported.
dashboard.what_if_d_note_solar_spread_evenly_over_: The solar energy is assumed to be spread evenly over each session.
dashboard.what_if_d_note_home_battery_kept_as_reco: The home battery is kept as recorded: its energy is neither replaced nor valued.
dashboard.what_if_d_note_replanned_without_solar_n: Charging replanned without solar is not modelled: it needs hourly solar availability, which is not stored.
dashboard.what_if_d_note_no_solar_production_not_m: No solar production at all is not modelled.
dashboard.what_if_d_note_recorded_sessions_only: Only charging sessions CJP recorded are used. Charging at other chargers cannot be seen.
dashboard.economy_explain: *Avg.: the average price while the car was plugged in. Daily: like most smart chargers – cheapest until the next departure (work plan), without waiting for a cheaper night. Lowest: the cheapest hours of the whole time plugged in (knows every price beforehand, so 100 % is close to impossible). Score: how close the price came to the lowest, measured from the average (100 % = the cheapest hours, 0 % = the average price). {valuta}/{distance}: all charging incl. public divided by the {distance} driven. The comparison only exists for periods with known plug-in times (from the last 30 days on).*
dashboard.drive_temperature_fit_1: For every degree colder the car drives
dashboard.drive_temperature_fit_2: less ({distance} per kWh from the battery):
dashboard.drive_temperature_no_data: Too few drives with a temperature yet – at least 5 drives at different temperatures are needed
dashboard.departures_met_1: The car had the required battery level at
dashboard.departures_no_data: No departures saved yet – they are saved from now on at every work plan departure
dashboard.learn_distance_on: *Learn driving distance* is on: the plan uses the higher of the entered and the learned value once there are enough days. The entered values are not changed.
dashboard.learn_distance_off: *Learn driving distance* is off: the learned values are only a suggestion, the plan uses the entered ones.
dashboard.learn_distance_no_data: No days measured yet – the odometer is read every evening at 23:59, the first day's distance comes after two evenings
dashboard.learn_distance_explain: *Every evening at 23:59 the odometer is read, and the day's distance is the difference to the evening before. Evenings CJP did not read itself (e.g. a restart or a new install) come from Home Assistant's long-term statistics of the odometer, or its history. Entered: the value in the work plan and under optimal weekly charging (*Settings*), which the plan uses. Learned: the median of that weekday over the last 8 weeks, rounded up to 5 {distance}, so one long trip doesn't move it. For the typical daily distance it is the 75th percentile of all days. Days: the number of measured days, ⏳ = too few to be used (at least 3 of the weekday and 14 in total). With *Learn driving distance* on, the plan uses the higher of the entered and the learned value once there are enough days, so a higher entered day still counts. The entered values are not changed.*
dashboard.planned_summary_3: of it outside the plan (manual, forced charging etc.):
dashboard.planned_no_data: No days saved yet – the plan for the next day is saved from now on every evening at 23:59
dashboard.capacity_title: kWh from the charger per 1 % per month
dashboard.capacity_explain: *If the number rises over the years, the battery holds less (or the charging loss rose). In winter it is higher, because the car uses energy to heat the battery. So compare the same month year by year and the same power group.*
dashboard.drive_temperature_explain: *Every drive from unplugging to plugging in again, with the outdoor temperature (the mean while the car was away) and {distance_kwh} from the odometer and the battery level (with the battery size set in CJP). The orange line is the average per 5 °C. The fit shows how much {distance_kwh} changes per degree and what the cold costs. Drives under 5 {distance} or under 2 % battery are left out. The first time the drives of the recorder's history (the last days) are read, from then on every drive is recorded.*
dashboard.departures_explain: *At every departure of the work plan the battery level the car left with is compared with the requirement: the day's driving plus the daily minimum level (✅ = met). The plan's target is the level the plan aimed for before work. Only departures from now on are saved (the plans of the past are not kept), the last 14 are shown.*
dashboard.planned_explain: *Every evening at 23:59 the kWh the plan expects to charge the next day are saved. Here they are compared with what was actually charged that day. Outside the plan = manual charging, charging because the battery was low and other charging. Public charging is not counted.*
dashboard.price_forecast_intro: The price integration's forecast against the real price, the last 30 days:
dashboard.price_forecast_unit: Error and bias in {valuta_kwh}. In brackets: the extra price per kWh of picking the hours by the forecast.
dashboard.price_forecast_no_data: Collected from now on: the first numbers at 13:00 tomorrow, when the real prices of the day after come.
dashboard.price_forecast_correction_off: The correction of the price forecast is off (*Settings → Advanced*).
dashboard.price_forecast_correction_waiting: The forecast is corrected per day ahead after 7 days of measurements.
dashboard.price_forecast_explain: Every hour CJP saves the buy price from the price integration's forecast (without CJP's own adder per day ahead) for the coming days. When the real prices of a day arrive (around 13:00 the day before), they are compared with what the forecast said 1, 2, 3 … days before. **Error** is the average deviation per hour, **Bias** > 0: the forecast was too high. **Cheapest found**: how many of the day's 4 cheapest hours by the forecast really were among the 4 cheapest – the hours the plan prefers to charge the car in. The extra price in brackets is what picking by the forecast instead of the real hours cost per kWh. The chart shows the real prices and the forecasts of the last and the coming days.
dashboard.price_forecast_correction_explain: **Correction**: with *Correct the price forecast* on (*Settings → Advanced*), the plan adds the correction to the forecast prices: minus the bias of the last 30 days for that day ahead, after 7 days of measurements and at most ±0.50 {valuta}. The chart shows the forecast the plan uses for the coming hours.
dashboard.soc_power_explain: The graph and table show learned power caps by 10% SOC band and phase; the table also shows sessions with stable measurements and those meeting the taper rule. Phase groups come from CJP's recorded per-phase amp settings, not separate current measurements on each physical phase. A SOC band gets a cap only when power is at least 10% lower than in a lower-SOC band in the same session, in at least 3 separate sessions. This comparison reduces, but cannot remove, the influence of the charger, solar or site limits. Unstable readings, unknown phases and bands without enough data leave the existing capacity assumption unchanged. The plan limits a price interval to the learned cap for the SOC bands it crosses, still subject to the existing charger and site capacity. Until a band has its own measurements, stable hourly long-term statistics give start values, marked 📊; they only count where the phase count is certain (a 1-phase charger, or above 3.8 kW on a 3-phase charger). This is a planning estimate only; it does not control the charger. The switch turns the use of the caps in the plan on or off; the measurements are collected either way.
dashboard.forecast_consumption_intro: House consumption per hour in kWh
dashboard.forecast_better: ⭐ {best} forecast the house consumption best the last 30 days: on average {best_mae} kWh off per hour against {selected_mae} kWh for the selected ✅ {selected} ({percent} % less error). The actual consumption was {actual} kWh per hour; {best} expected {best_forecast} kWh and {selected} {selected_forecast} kWh. With *Choose the forecast type automatically* on, the most accurate type is used by itself.
dashboard.forecast_better_drives: ⭐ {best} forecast the car's {distance_kwh} best on the last drives: on average {best_mae} {distance_kwh} off per drive against {selected_mae} {distance_kwh} for the selected ✅ {selected} ({percent} % less error). The car actually drove {actual} {distance_kwh}; {best} expected {best_forecast} {distance_kwh} and {selected} {selected_forecast} {distance_kwh}. With *Choose the forecast type automatically* on, the most accurate type is used by itself.
dashboard.forecast_auto_on: 🔄 The forecast type is chosen automatically: the house consumption now uses ✅ {selected}, the most accurate the last 30 days. It only switches when another type has at least 5 % less error.
dashboard.forecast_auto_on_drives: 🔄 The forecast type is chosen automatically: the {distance_kwh} now uses ✅ {selected}, the most accurate on the last drives. It only switches when another type has at least 5 % less error.
dashboard.forecast_auto_waiting: 🔄 The automatic choice for the house consumption starts after {days} days of measurements. Until then the selected ✅ {manual} is used.
dashboard.forecast_auto_waiting_drives: 🔄 The automatic choice for the {distance_kwh} starts after {drives} drives. Until then the selected ✅ {manual} is used.
dashboard.forecast_no_data: Collected from now on: the house consumption after the first whole day, {distance_kwh} after the first drive.
dashboard.forecast_explain:
Just before a new measurement is added to the history (the house consumption every hour, the car's {distance_kwh} after every drive), CJP calculates what each forecast type would have predicted from the same history and compares it with the measurement. ✅ the forecast type in use, ⭐ the most accurate. **Avg.** is what each type expected on average, against the actual value at the top. The **error** is counted hour by hour / drive by drive, so a type can hit the average and still miss a lot each time. **Bias** > 0: the forecast was too high.

The forecast type (*Settings → Advanced → Forecast type*) applies to the house consumption, {distance_kwh} and the fallback prices alike, so pick the one that is most accurate where it matters most. With *Choose the forecast type automatically* on, the house consumption and {distance_kwh} each use their most accurate type instead (after 7 days of measurements / 10 drives) and only switch when another type has at least 5 % less error; the fallback prices and the solar history keep the selected type. The house consumption is only used for the solar surplus; {distance_kwh} for how much trips and workdays need.
dashboard.history_explain:
* **Battery level and charging limit**: the last 48 hours (and the simulated battery level when it is on).
* **Driving efficiency**: the last 30 days.
* **Charged by solar**: the last 7 days.
